operations.description: Performs an authorization check for the currently authenticated user.

params.name: permissionName
params.description: String value representing the permission name to check for.

params.name: resourceName
params.description: String value for the name of the resource to check permissions for.

params.name: resourceType
params.description:
An integer representing the resource type to check permissions for.
See the [User Guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/authorization-service/#resources)
for a list of integer representations of resource types.

params.name: resourceId
params.description:
The id of the resource to check permissions for. If left blank,
a check for global permissions on the resource is performed.

params.name: userId
params.description:
The id of the user to check permissions for. The currently authenticated
user must have a READ permission for the Authorization resource. If `userId` is
blank, a check for the currently authenticated user is performed.

operations.description:
Requests the number of batches that fulfill the query criteria.
Takes the same filtering parameters as the [Get Batches](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/batch/get-query/) method.

params.name: batchId
params.description: Filter by batch id.

params.name: type
params.description:
Filter by batch type.
See the [User Guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/batch/#creating-a-batch)
for more information about batch types.

params.name: tenantIdIn
params.description: Filter by a comma-separated list of `Strings`. A batch matches if it has one of the given tenant ids.

params.name: withoutTenantId
params.description:
Only include batches which belong to no tenant.
Value can effectively only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: suspended
params.description:
A `Boolean` value which indicates whether only active or suspended batches should be included.
When the value is set to `true`, only suspended batches will be returned and
when the value is set to `false`, only active batches will be returned.

params.name: createdBy
params.description: Only include batches that were started by this user id.

params.name: startedBefore
params.description:
Only include batches that were started before the given date. By [default](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/overview/date-format/),
the date must have the format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, e.g., `2013-01-23T14:42:45.000+0200`.

params.name: startedAfter
params.description:
Only include batches that were started after the given date. By [default](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/overview/date-format/),
the date must have the format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, e.g., `2013-01-23T14:42:45.000+0200`.

params.name: withFailures
params.description:
Only include batches having jobs with failures.
Value can only be `true`.

params.name: withoutFailures
params.description:
Only include batches having jobs without failures.
Value can only be `true`.

fields.name: suspended
fields.description:
A Boolean value which indicates whether to activate or suspend a given instance 
(e.g. process instance, job, job definition, or batch). When the value is set to true, 
the given instance will be suspended and when the value is set to false, 
the given instance will be activated.

operations.summary: Evaluate conditional start events and start process instances
operations.description:
Triggers evaluation of conditions for conditional start event(s). 
Internally this maps to the engines condition evaluation builder method ConditionEvaluationBuilder#evaluateStartConditions(). 
For more information see the [Conditional Start Events](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/bpmn20/events/conditional-events/#conditional-start-event)
section of the [BPMN 2.0 Implementation Reference](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/bpmn20/).

fields.name: businessKey
fields.description: Used for the process instances that have been triggered after the evaluation.

fields.name: tenantId
fields.description:
Used to evaluate a condition for a tenant with the given id.
Will only evaluate conditions of process definitions which belong to the tenant.

fields.name: withoutTenantId
fields.description:
A Boolean value that indicates whether the conditions should only be evaluated of process definitions which belong to no tenant or not.
Value may only be true, as false is the default behavior.

fields.name: processDefinitionId
fields.description: Used to evaluate conditions of the process definition with the given id.

operations.name: evaluate

operations.description:
Requests the number of decision definitions that fulfill the query criteria.
Takes the same filtering parameters as the
[Get Decision Definition](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/decision-definition/get-query/) method.

params.name: decisionDefinitionId
params.description: Filter by decision definition id.

params.name: decisionDefinitionIdIn
params.description: Filter by decision definition ids.

params.name: name
params.description: Filter by decision definition name.

params.name: nameLike
params.description: Filter by decision definition names that the parameter is a substring of.

params.name: deploymentId
params.description: Filter by the deployment the id belongs to.

params.name: deployedAfter
params.description:
Filter by the deploy time of the deployment the decision definition belongs to.
Only selects decision definitions that have been deployed after (exclusive) a specific time.

params.name: deployedAt
params.description:
Filter by the deploy time of the deployment the decision definition belongs to.
Only selects decision definitions that have been deployed at a specific time (exact match).

params.name: key
params.description: Filter by decision definition key, i.e., the id in the DMN 1.0 XML. Exact match.

params.name: keyLike
params.description: Filter by decision definition keys that the parameter is a substring of.

params.name: category
params.description: Filter by decision definition category. Exact match.

params.name: categoryLike
params.description: Filter by decision definition categories that the parameter is a substring of.

params.name: version
params.description: Filter by decision definition version.

params.name: latestVersion
params.description:
Only include those decision definitions that are latest versions.
Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: resourceName
params.description: Filter by the name of the decision definition resource. Exact match.

params.name: resourceNameLike
params.description: Filter by names of those decision definition resources that the parameter is a substring of.

params.name: decisionRequirementsDefinitionId
params.description: Filter by the id of the decision requirements definition this decision definition belongs to.

params.name: decisionRequirementsDefinitionKey
params.description: Filter by the key of the decision requirements definition this decision definition belongs to.

params.name: withoutDecisionRequirementsDefinition
params.description:
Only include decision definitions which does not belongs to any decision requirements definition.
Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: tenantIdIn
params.description: Filter by a comma-separated list of `Strings`. A decision definition must have one of the given tenant ids.

params.name: withoutTenantId
params.description:
Only include decision definitions which belong to no tenant.
Value can effectively only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: includeDecisionDefinitionsWithoutTenantId
params.description:
Include decision definitions which belong to no tenant.
Can be used in combination with `tenantIdIn`.
Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: versionTag
params.description: Filter by the version tag.

params.name: versionTagLike
params.description: Filter by the version tags of those decision definition resources that the parameter is a substring of.

operations.description:
Creates a deployment.

**Security Consideration**

Deployments can contain custom code in form of scripts or EL expressions to customize process behavior.
This may be abused for remote execution of arbitrary code.

fields.name: tenant-id
fields.description: The tenant id for the deployment to be created.

fields.name: deployment-source
fields.description: The source for the deployment to be created.

fields.name: deploy-changed-only
fields.description:
A flag indicating whether the process engine should perform duplicate checking on a per-resource basis.
If set to true, only those resources that have actually changed are deployed.
Checks are made against resources included previous deployments of the same name and source and only against the latest versions of those resources.
If set to true, the option enable-duplicate-filtering is overridden and set to true.

fields.name: enable-duplicate-filtering
fields.description:
A flag indicating whether the process engine should perform duplicate checking for the deployment or not.
This allows you to check if a deployment with the same name and the same resouces already exists and
if true, not create a new deployment but instead return the existing deployment. The default value is false.

fields.name: deployment-name
fields.description: The name for the deployment to be created.

fields.name: deployment-activation-time
fields.description:
Sets the date on which the process definitions contained in this deployment will be activated. This means that all process
definitions will be deployed as usual, but they will be suspended from the start until the given activation date.
By [default](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/overview/date-format/),
the date must have the format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, e.g., `2013-01-23T14:42:45.000+0200`.

params.name: deserializeValue
params.description:
Determines whether serializable variable values (typically
variables that store custom Java objects) should be deserialized
on server side (default `true`).

If set to `true`, a serializable variable will be deserialized on
server side and transformed to JSON using
[Jackson's](https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson) POJO/bean
property introspection feature. Note that this requires the Java
classes of the variable value to be on the REST API's classpath.
If set to `false`, a serializable variable will be returned in its
serialized format. For example, a variable that is serialized as
XML will be returned as a JSON string containing XML.

**Note:** While `true` is the default value for reasons of
backward compatibility, we recommend setting this parameter to
`false` when developing web applications that are independent of
the Java process applications deployed to the engine.

[default](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/overview/date-format/), the date must have the format

operations.summary: Report a failure of an external task
operations.description:
Reports a failure to execute an external task by id. A number of retries and a timeout until the task can
be retried can be specified. If retries are set to 0, an incident for this task is created.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the external task to report a failure for.

fields.name: errorMessage
fields.description: An message indicating the reason of the failure.

fields.name: errorDetails
fields.description: A detailed error description.

fields.name: retries
fields.description:
A number of how often the task should be retried. Must be >= 0. If this is 0, an incident is created and
the task cannot be fetched anymore unless the retries are increased again. The incident's message is set
to the `errorMessage` parameter.

fields.name: retryTimeout
fields.description: A timeout in milliseconds before the external task becomes available again for fetching. Must be >= 0.

fields.name: workerId
fields.description:
**Mandatory.** The ID of the worker who is performing the operation on the external task.

Retrieves a report about a historic batch operations relevant to history cleanup
(see
[History cleanup](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/history/#history-cleanup)
) so that you can tune the history time to live.
These reports include the count of the finished batches, cleanable
batches and type of the batch.
The size of the result set can be retrieved by using the
[Get Cleanable Batch Report Count](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/history/batch/get-cleanable-batch-report-count/)
method.

**Please note:**
The history time to live for batch operations does not support [Multi-Tenancy](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/multi-tenancy.md).
The report will return an information for all batch operations (for all tenants) if you have permissions
to see the history.

Determines whether serializable variable values (typically

on server side (default `true`).

If set to `true`, a serializable variable will be deserialized on
server side and transformed to JSON using
[Jackson's](https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson) POJO/bean
property introspection feature. Note that this requires the Java
classes of the variable value to be on the REST API's classpath.

backward compatibility, we recommend setting this parameter to
`false` when developing web applications that are independent of
the Java process applications deployed to the engine.

operations.name: query-count

operations.description:
Retrieves historic statistics of a given process definition, grouped by activities.
These statistics include the number of running activity instances and,
optionally, the number of canceled activity instances, finished
activity instances and activity instances which completed a scope
(i.e., in BPMN 2.0 manner: a scope is completed by an activity
instance when the activity instance consumed a token but did not emit
a new token).
**Note:** This only includes historic data.

values are `true` or `false`. Default: `false`.

values are `true` or `false`. Default: `false`.

params.name: completeScope

or not. Valid values are `true` or `false`. Default: `false`.

params.description:
Only include process instances that have/had variables with certain values.
Variable filtering expressions are comma-separated and are structured as follows:
A valid parameter value has the form `key_operator_value`. `key` is the variable name, `operator` is the comparison operator to be used and `value` the variable value.

**Note:** Values are always treated as String objects on server side.

Valid operator values are: `eq` - equal to; `neq` - not equal to; `gt` - greater than; `gteq` - greater than or equal to; `lt` - lower than; `lteq` - lower than or equal to; `like`.

Key and value may not contain underscore or comma characters.

params.description: Match all variable names provided in variables case-insensitively. If set to `true` variableName and variablename are treated as equal.

params.name: variableValuesIgnoreCase
params.description: Match all variable values provided in variables case-insensitively. If set to `true` variableValue and variablevalue are treated as equal.

params.name: variables
params.description:
Only include process instances that have/had variables with certain values.
Variable filtering expressions are comma-separated and are structured as follows:
A valid parameter value has the form `key_operator_value`. `key` is the variable name, `operator` is the comparison operator to be used and `value` the variable value.

**Note:** Values are always treated as String objects on server side.

Valid operator values are: `eq` - equal to; `neq` - not equal to; `gt` - greater than; `gteq` - greater than or equal to; `lt` - lower than; `lteq` - lower than or equal to; `like`.

Key and value may not contain underscore or comma characters.

operations.summary: Set the removal time of historic process instances (batch)
operations.description:
Sets the removal time to multiple historic process instances asynchronously (batch).

At least `historicProcessInstanceIds` or `historicProcessInstanceQuery` has to be provided.
If both are provided, all instances matching query criterion and instances from the list will be updated with a removal time.

fields.name: historicProcessInstanceIds
fields.description: The id of the process instance.

fields.name: hierarchical
fields.description:
Sets the removal time to all historic process instances in the hierarchy.
Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

fields.name: updateInChunks
fields.description:
Handles removal time updates in chunks, taking into account the defined size in
`removalTimeUpdateChunkSize` in the process engine configuration. The size of the 
chunks can also be overridden per call with the `updateChunkSize` parameter.
Enabling this option can lead to multiple executions of the resulting jobs, preventing
the database transaction from timing out by limiting the number of rows to update.
Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

fields.name: updateChunkSize
fields.description:
Defines the size of the chunks in which removal time updates are processed.
The value must be a positive integer between `1` and `500`. This only has an 
effect if `updateInChunks` is set to `true`. If undefined, the operation uses the 
`removalTimeUpdateChunkSize` defined in the process engine configuration.

fields.name: absoluteRemovalTime
fields.description:
The date for which the instances shall be removed. Value may not be `null`.

**Note:** Cannot be set in conjunction with `clearedRemovalTime` or `calculatedRemovalTime`.

fields.name: clearedRemovalTime
fields.description:
Sets the removal time to `null`. Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

**Note:** Cannot be set in conjunction with `absoluteRemovalTime` or `calculatedRemovalTime`.

fields.name: calculatedRemovalTime
fields.description:
The removal time is calculated based on the engine's configuration settings. Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

**Note:** Cannot be set in conjunction with `absoluteRemovalTime` or `clearedRemovalTime`.

operations.name: count

operations.summary: Get a report of historic task instances
operations.description:
Retrieves a report of completed tasks. When the report type is set to `count`, the
report contains a list of completed task counts where an entry contains the task name, the
definition key of the task, the process definition id, the process definition key, the process
definition name and the count of how many tasks were completed for the specified key in a given
period. When the report type is set to `duration`, the report contains a minimum, maximum and
average duration value of all completed task instances in a given period.

params.name: reportType
params.description:
**Mandatory.** Specifies the kind of the report to execute. To retrieve a report
about the duration of process instances the value must be set to `duration`. For a
report of the completed tasks in a specific timespan the value must be set to `count`.

params.name: periodUnit
params.description:
When the report type is set to `duration`, this parameter is **mandatory**.
Specifies the granularity of the report. Valid values are `month` and `quarter`.

params.name: completedBefore
params.description:
Restrict to tasks that were completed before the given date. By [default](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/overview/date-format/),
the date must have the format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`,
e.g., `2013-01-23T14:42:45.000+0200`.

params.name: completedAfter
params.description:
Restrict to tasks that were completed after the given date. By [default](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/overview/date-format/),
the date must have the format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`,
e.g., `2013-01-23T14:42:45.000+0200`.

params.name: groupBy
params.description:
When the report type is set to `count`, this parameter is **mandatory**. Groups the
tasks report by a given criterion. Valid values are `taskName` and `processDefinition`.

[Get User Operation Log Count](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/history/user-operation-log/get-user-operation-log-query-count/)

restrictions on the entities they apply to. That means, if a single
process instance is updated, the field `processInstanceId` is

`null` restriction is viewed as a wildcard, i.e., matches a process
instance with any id) and the field `processDefinitionId` is
populated. This way, which entities were changed by a user operation
can easily be reconstructed.

params.description:
Determines whether serializable variable values (typically variables that
store custom Java objects) should be deserialized on server side (default
`true`).

If set to `true`, a serializable variable will be deserialized on server side
and transformed to JSON using
[Jackson's](https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson) POJO/bean property
introspection feature. Note that this requires the Java classes of the
variable value to be on the REST API's classpath.

If set to `false`, a serializable variable will be returned in its serialized
format. For example, a variable that is serialized as XML will be returned as
a JSON string containing XML.

**Note:** While `true` is the default value for reasons of backward
compatibility, we recommend setting this parameter to `false` when developing
web applications that are independent of the Java process applications
deployed to the engine.

This method takes the same message body as the
[Get Variable Instances (POST)](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/history/variable-instance/post-variable-instance-query/)
method and therefore it is more powerful regarding variable values
than the
[Get Variable Instance Count](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/history/variable-instance/get-variable-instance-query-count/)
method.

fields.name: variableName
fields.description: Filter by variable name.

fields.name: variableNameLike
fields.description: Restrict to variables with a name like the parameter.

fields.name: variableNamesIgnoreCase
fields.description:
Match the variable name provided in `variableName` and `variableNameLike` case-
insensitively. If set to `true` **variableName** and **variablename** are
treated as equal.

fields.name: variableValuesIgnoreCase
fields.description:
Match the variable value provided in `variableValue` case-insensitively. If set to `true`
**variableValue** and **variablevalue** are treated as equal.

fields.name: variableTypeIn
fields.description:
Only include historic variable instances which belong to one of the passed and comma-
separated variable types. A list of all supported variable types can be found
[here](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/variables/#supported-variable-values).
**Note:** All non-primitive variables are associated with the type
'serializable'.

Takes the same parameters as the [Get
Jobs](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/job/get-query/) method.

params.name: jobId
params.description: Filter by job id.

params.name: jobIds
params.description: Filter by a comma-separated list of job ids.

params.name: jobDefinitionId
params.description: Only select jobs which exist for the given job definition.

params.name: processInstanceId
params.description: Only select jobs which exist for the given process instance.

params.name: processInstanceIds
params.description: Only select jobs which exist for the given comma-separated list of process instance ids.

params.name: executionId
params.description: Only select jobs which exist for the given execution.

params.name: processDefinitionId
params.description: Filter by the id of the process definition the jobs run on.

params.name: processDefinitionKey
params.description: Filter by the key of the process definition the jobs run on.

params.name: activityId
params.description: Only select jobs which exist for an activity with the given id.

params.name: withRetriesLeft
params.description:
Only select jobs which have retries left. Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the
default behavior.

params.name: executable
params.description:
Only select jobs which are executable, i.e., retries > 0 and due date is `null` or due
date is in the past. Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default
behavior.

params.name: timers
params.description:
Only select jobs that are timers. Cannot be used together with `messages`. Value may only
be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: messages
params.description:
Only select jobs that are messages. Cannot be used together with `timers`. Value may only
be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: dueDates
params.description:
Only select jobs where the due date is lower or higher than the given date.
Due date expressions are comma-separated and are structured as follows:

A valid condition value has the form `operator_value`.
`operator` is the comparison operator to be used and `value` the date value
as string.

Valid operator values are: `gt` - greater than; `lt` - lower than.
`value` may not contain underscore or comma characters.

params.name: createTimes
params.description:
Only select jobs created before or after the given date.

Create time expressions are comma-separated and are structured as
follows:

A valid condition value has the form `operator_value`.
`operator` is the comparison operator to be used and `value` the date value
as string.

Valid operator values are: `gt` - greater than; `lt` - lower than.
`value` may not contain underscore or comma characters.

params.name: withException
params.description:
Only select jobs that failed due to an exception. Value may only be `true`, as `false` is
the default behavior.

params.name: exceptionMessage
params.description: Only select jobs that failed due to an exception with the given message.

params.name: failedActivityId
params.description: Only select jobs that failed due to an exception at an activity with the given id.

params.name: noRetriesLeft
params.description:
Only select jobs which have no retries left. Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the
default behavior.

params.name: active
params.description: Only include active jobs. Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: suspended
params.description: Only include suspended jobs. Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: priorityLowerThanOrEquals
params.description:
Only include jobs with a priority lower than or equal to the given value. Value must be a
valid `long` value.

params.name: priorityHigherThanOrEquals
params.description:
Only include jobs with a priority higher than or equal to the given value. Value must be a
valid `long` value.

params.name: tenantIdIn
params.description: Only include jobs which belong to one of the passed comma-separated tenant ids.

params.name: withoutTenantId
params.description:
Only include jobs which belong to no tenant. Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the
default behavior.

params.name: includeJobsWithoutTenantId
params.description:
Include jobs which belong to no tenant. Can be used in combination with `tenantIdIn`.
Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: acquired
params.description:
Only select jobs which are acquired, i.e.,  lock expiration date is not null, lock expiration
date is in future. Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default
behavior. This does not take account if the job is suspended. This filter can be used with the
suspension filter.

fields.name: jobId
fields.description: Filter by job id.

fields.name: jobIds
fields.description: Filter by a  list of job ids.

fields.name: jobDefinitionId
fields.description: Only select jobs which exist for the given job definition.

fields.name: processInstanceId
fields.description: Only select jobs which exist for the given process instance.

fields.name: processInstanceIds
fields.description: Only select jobs which exist for the given  list of process instance ids.

fields.name: executionId
fields.description: Only select jobs which exist for the given execution.

fields.name: processDefinitionId
fields.description: Filter by the id of the process definition the jobs run on.

fields.name: processDefinitionKey
fields.description: Filter by the key of the process definition the jobs run on.

fields.name: activityId
fields.description: Only select jobs which exist for an activity with the given id.

fields.name: withRetriesLeft
fields.description:
Only select jobs which have retries left. Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the
default behavior.

fields.name: executable
fields.description:
Only select jobs which are executable, i.e., retries > 0 and due date is `null` or due
date is in the past. Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default
behavior.

fields.name: timers
fields.description:
Only select jobs that are timers. Cannot be used together with `messages`. Value may only
be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

fields.name: messages
fields.description:
Only select jobs that are messages. Cannot be used together with `timers`. Value may only
be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

fields.name: withException
fields.description:
Only select jobs that failed due to an exception. Value may only be `true`, as `false` is
the default behavior.

fields.name: exceptionMessage
fields.description: Only select jobs that failed due to an exception with the given message.

fields.name: failedActivityId
fields.description: Only select jobs that failed due to an exception at an activity with the given id.

fields.name: noRetriesLeft
fields.description:
Only select jobs which have no retries left. Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the
default behavior.

fields.name: active
fields.description: Only include active jobs. Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

fields.name: suspended
fields.description: Only include suspended jobs. Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

fields.name: priorityLowerThanOrEquals
fields.description:
Only include jobs with a priority lower than or equal to the given value. Value must be a
valid `long` value.

fields.name: priorityHigherThanOrEquals
fields.description:
Only include jobs with a priority higher than or equal to the given value. Value must be a
valid `long` value.

fields.name: tenantIdIn
fields.description: Only include jobs which belong to one of the passed  tenant ids.

fields.name: withoutTenantId
fields.description:
Only include jobs which belong to no tenant. Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the
default behavior.

fields.name: includeJobsWithoutTenantId
fields.description:
Include jobs which belong to no tenant. Can be used in combination with `tenantIdIn`.
Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

fields.name: acquired
fields.description:
Only select jobs which are acquired, i.e.,  lock expiration date is not null, lock expiration
date is in future. Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default
behavior. This does not take account if the job is suspended. This filter can be used with the
suspension filter.

operations.summary: Set Job Definition Priority by Id
operations.description:
Sets an overriding execution priority for jobs with the given definition id.
Optionally, the priorities of all the definitions' existing jobs are
updated accordingly. The priority can be reset by setting it to
`null`, meaning that a new job's priority will not be determined based
on its definition's priority any longer. See the
[user guide on job prioritization](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/the-job-executor/#set-job-definition-priorities-via-managementservice-api)
for details.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the job definition to be updated.

fields.name: priority
fields.description:
The new execution priority number for jobs of the given definition. The
definition's priority can be reset by using the value `null`. In
that case, the job definition's priority no longer applies but a new
job's priority is determined as specified in the process model.

fields.name: includeJobs
fields.description:
A boolean value indicating whether existing jobs of the given definition should
receive the priority as well. Default value is `false`. Can only be
`true` when the __priority__ parameter is not `null`.

responses.description: Request successful. This method returns no content.

operations.summary: Correlate a message to process instances or start events
operations.description:
Correlates a message to the process engine to either trigger a message start event or an intermediate message 
catching event. Internally this maps to the engine's message correlation builder methods
`MessageCorrelationBuilder#correlateWithResult()` and `MessageCorrelationBuilder#correlateAllWithResult()`.
For more information about the correlation behavior, see the [Message Events](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/bpmn20/events/message-events/)
section of the [BPMN 2.0 Implementation Reference](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/bpmn20/).

fields.name: messageName
fields.description: The name of the message to deliver.

fields.name: businessKey
fields.description:
Used for correlation of process instances that wait for incoming messages.
Will only correlate to executions that belong to a process instance with the provided business key.

fields.name: tenantId
fields.description:
Used to correlate the message for a tenant with the given id.
Will only correlate to executions and process definitions which belong to the tenant.
Must not be supplied in conjunction with a `withoutTenantId`.

fields.name: withoutTenantId
fields.description:
A Boolean value that indicates whether the message should only be correlated to executions
and process definitions which belong to no tenant or not. Value may only be `true`, as `false`
is the default behavior.
Must not be supplied in conjunction with a `tenantId`.

fields.name: processInstanceId
fields.description: Used to correlate the message to the process instance with the given id.

fields.name: all
fields.description:
A Boolean value that indicates whether the message should be correlated to exactly one entity or multiple entities.
If the value is set to `false`, the message will be correlated to exactly one entity (execution or process definition).
If the value is set to `true`, the message will be correlated to multiple executions and a process definition that
can be instantiated by this message in one go.

fields.name: resultEnabled
fields.description:
A Boolean value that indicates whether the result of the correlation should be returned or not.
If this property is set to `true`, there will be returned a list of message correlation result objects. Depending on the
all property, there will be either one ore more returned results in the list.

The default value is `false`, which means no result will be returned.

fields.name: variablesInResultEnabled
fields.description:
A Boolean value that indicates whether the result of the correlation should contain process variables or not.
The parameter resultEnabled should be set to `true` in order to use this it.

The default value is `false`, which means the variables will not be returned.

responses.description:
Request successful. The property `resultEnabled` in the request body was `true`.
The `variables` property is only returned, if the property variablesInResultEnable`
was set to `true` in the request.
Request successful. The property `resultEnabled` in the request body was `false` (Default).

fields.description:

the process definitions with the given key.
When the value is set to `true`, all process instances of the process definitions with the given key
will be activated or suspended and when the value is set to `false`, the suspension state of

the date must have the format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, e.g., `2013-01-23T14:42:45.000+0200`.

operations.description:
Requests the number of process definitions that fulfill the query criteria.
Takes the same filtering parameters as the [Get Definitions](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/process-definition/get-query/) method.

params.name: processDefinitionId
params.description: Filter by process definition id.

params.name: processDefinitionIdIn
params.description: Filter by a comma-separated list of process definition ids.

params.name: name
params.description: Filter by process definition name.

params.name: nameLike
params.description: Filter by process definition names that the parameter is a substring of.

params.name: deploymentId
params.description: Filter by the deployment the id belongs to.

params.name: deployedAfter
params.description:
Filter by the deploy time of the deployment the process definition belongs to.
Only selects process definitions that have been deployed after (exclusive) a specific time.
By [default](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/overview/date-format/), the date must have the
format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, e.g.,
`2013-01-23T14:42:45.546+0200`.

params.name: deployedAt
params.description:
Filter by the deploy time of the deployment the process definition belongs to.
Only selects process definitions that have been deployed at a specific time (exact match).
By [default](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/overview/date-format/), the date must have the
format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, e.g.,
`2013-01-23T14:42:45.546+0200`.

params.name: key
params.description: Filter by process definition key, i.e., the id in the BPMN 2.0 XML. Exact match.

params.name: keysIn
params.description: Filter by a comma-separated list of process definition keys.

params.name: keyLike
params.description: Filter by process definition keys that the parameter is a substring of.

params.name: category
params.description: Filter by process definition category. Exact match.

params.name: categoryLike
params.description: Filter by process definition categories that the parameter is a substring of.

params.name: version
params.description: Filter by process definition version.

params.name: latestVersion
params.description:
Only include those process definitions that are latest versions.
Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: resourceName
params.description: Filter by the name of the process definition resource. Exact match.

params.name: resourceNameLike
params.description: Filter by names of those process definition resources that the parameter is a substring of.

params.name: startableBy
params.description: Filter by a user name who is allowed to start the process.

params.name: active
params.description:
Only include active process definitions.
Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: suspended
params.description:
Only include suspended process definitions.
Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: incidentId
params.description: Filter by the incident id.

params.name: incidentType
params.description:
Filter by the incident type.
See the [User Guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/incidents/#incident-types)
for a list of incident types.

params.name: incidentMessage
params.description: Filter by the incident message. Exact match.

params.name: incidentMessageLike
params.description: Filter by the incident message that the parameter is a substring of.

params.name: tenantIdIn
params.description:
Filter by a comma-separated list of tenant ids.
A process definition must have one of the given tenant ids.

params.name: withoutTenantId
params.description:
Only include process definitions which belong to no tenant.
Value may only be true, as false is the default behavior.

params.name: includeProcessDefinitionsWithoutTenantId
params.description:
Include process definitions which belong to no tenant. Can be used in combination with `tenantIdIn`.
Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: versionTag
params.description: Filter by the version tag.

params.name: versionTagLike
params.description: Filter by the version tag that the parameter is a substring of.

params.name: withoutVersionTag
params.description: Only include process definitions without a `versionTag`.

params.name: startableInTasklist
params.description: Filter by process definitions which are startable in Tasklist..

params.name: notStartableInTasklist
params.description: Filter by process definitions which are not startable in Tasklist.

params.name: startablePermissionCheck
params.description:
Filter by process definitions which the user is allowed to start in Tasklist.
If the user doesn't have these permissions the result will be empty list.
The permissions are:
* `CREATE` permission for all Process instances
* `CREATE_INSTANCE` and `READ` permission on Process definition level

operations.description:
Retrieves runtime statistics of a given process definition, grouped by activities.
These statistics include the number of running activity instances, optionally the number of failed jobs
and also optionally the number of incidents either grouped by incident types or for a specific incident type.
**Note**: This does not include historic data.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the process definition.

params.name: failedJobs
params.description: Whether to include the number of failed jobs in the result or not. Valid values are `true` or `false`.

params.name: incidents
params.description:
Valid values for this property are `true` or `false`.
If this property has been set to `true` the result will include the corresponding number of incidents
for each occurred incident type.
If it is set to `false`, the incidents will not be included in the result.
Cannot be used in combination with `incidentsForType`.

will only include the number of incidents for the assigned incident type.
Cannot be used in combination with `incidents`.
See the [User Guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/incidents/#incident-types)
for a list of incident types.

operations.description:
Retrieves the start form variables for a process definition
(only if they are defined via the 
[Generated Task Form](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/task-forms/#generated-task-forms) approach).
The start form variables take form data specified on the start event into account.
If form fields are defined, the variable types and default values
of the form fields are taken into account.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the process definition to retrieve the variables for.

params.name: variableNames
params.description:
A comma-separated list of variable names. Allows restricting the list of requested
variables to the variable names in the list. It is best practice to restrict the
list of variables to the variables actually required by the form in order to
minimize fetching of data. If the query parameter is ommitted all variables are
fetched. If the query parameter contains non-existent variable names, the variable
names are ignored.

params.name: deserializeValues
params.description:
Determines whether serializable variable values (typically variables that store
custom Java objects) should be deserialized on server side (default true).

If set to true, a serializable variable will be deserialized on server side and
transformed to JSON using [Jackson's](http://jackson.codehaus.org/) POJO/bean
property introspection feature. Note that this requires the Java classes of the
variable value to be on the REST API's classpath.

If set to false, a serializable variable will be returned in its serialized format.
For example, a variable that is serialized as XML will be returned as a JSON string
containing XML.

**Note**: While true is the default value for reasons of backward compatibility, we
recommend setting this parameter to false when developing web applications that are
independent of the Java process applications deployed to the engine.

responses.description: Request successful. A JSON object containing a property for each variable returned.

custom Java objects) should be deserialized on server side (default true).

If set to true, a serializable variable will be deserialized on server side and
transformed to JSON using [Jackson's](http://jackson.codehaus.org/) POJO/bean
property introspection feature. Note that this requires the Java classes of the
variable value to be on the REST API's classpath.

If set to false, a serializable variable will be returned in its serialized format.
For example, a variable that is serialized as XML will be returned as a JSON string
containing XML.

**Note**: While true is the default value for reasons of backward compatibility, we
recommend setting this parameter to false when developing web applications that are
independent of the Java process applications deployed to the engine.

to
the `CalledProcessDefinition` interface in the engine. The list
contains all process definitions
that are referenced statically by call activities in the given
process. This endpoint does not

operations.description:
Retrieves runtime statistics of the process engine, grouped by process definitions.
These statistics include the number of running process instances, optionally the number of failed jobs
and also optionally the number of incidents either grouped by incident types or
for a specific incident type.
**Note**: This does not include historic data.

params.name: failedJobs
params.description: Whether to include the number of failed jobs in the result or not. Valid values are `true` or `false`.

params.name: incidents
params.description:
Valid values for this property are `true` or `false`.
If this property has been set to `true` the result will include the corresponding number of incidents
for each occurred incident type.
If it is set to `false`, the incidents will not be included in the result.
Cannot be used in combination with `incidentsForType`.

params.name: incidentsForType
params.description:
If this property has been set with any incident type (i.e., a string value) the result
will only include the number of incidents for the assigned incident type.
Cannot be used in combination with `incidents`.
See the [User Guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/incidents/#incident-types)
for a list of incident types.

params.name: rootIncidents
params.description:
Valid values for this property are `true` or `false`.
If this property has been set to `true` the result will include the corresponding number of
root incidents for each occurred incident type.
If it is set to `false`, the incidents will not be included in the result.
Cannot be used in combination with `incidentsForType` or `incidents`.

operations.description:
Queries for process definitions that fulfill given parameters. Parameters may be the properties of 
process definitions, such as the name, key or version. The size of the result set can be retrieved
by using the [Get Definition Count](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/process-definition/get-query-count/) method.

params.description: Filter by process definition name.

params.name: nameLike
params.description: Filter by process definition names that the parameter is a substring of.

params.name: deploymentId
params.description: Filter by the deployment the id belongs to.

params.name: deployedAfter
params.description:
Filter by the deploy time of the deployment the process definition belongs to.
Only selects process definitions that have been deployed after (exclusive) a specific time.
By [default](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/overview/date-format/), the date must have the
format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, e.g.,
`2013-01-23T14:42:45.546+0200`.

params.name: deployedAt
params.description:
Filter by the deploy time of the deployment the process definition belongs to.
Only selects process definitions that have been deployed at a specific time (exact match).
By [default](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/overview/date-format/), the date must have the
format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, e.g.,
`2013-01-23T14:42:45.546+0200`.

params.name: key
params.description: Filter by process definition key, i.e., the id in the BPMN 2.0 XML. Exact match.

params.name: keysIn
params.description: Filter by a comma-separated list of process definition keys.

params.name: keyLike
params.description: Filter by process definition keys that the parameter is a substring of.

params.description: Filter by process definition category. Exact match.

params.name: categoryLike
params.description: Filter by process definition categories that the parameter is a substring of.

params.name: version
params.description: Filter by process definition version.

params.name: latestVersion
params.description:
Only include those process definitions that are latest versions.

params.name: resourceName
params.description: Filter by the name of the process definition resource. Exact match.

params.name: resourceNameLike
params.description: Filter by names of those process definition resources that the parameter is a substring of.

params.name: startableBy
params.description: Filter by a user name who is allowed to start the process.

params.name: active
params.description:
Only include active process definitions.
Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: suspended
params.description:
Only include suspended process definitions.
Value may only be `true`, as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: incidentId
params.description: Filter by the incident id.

params.name: incidentType
params.description:
Filter by the incident type.
See the [User Guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/incidents/#incident-types)
for a list of incident types.

params.name: incidentMessage
params.description: Filter by the incident message. Exact match.

params.name: incidentMessageLike

params.name: withoutTenantId

params.name: includeProcessDefinitionsWithoutTenantId
params.description:

params.name: versionTagLike

params.name: withoutVersionTag
params.description: Only include process definitions without a `versionTag`.

params.name: startableInTasklist
params.description: Filter by process definitions which are startable in Tasklist..

params.name: notStartableInTasklist
params.description: Filter by process definitions which are not startable in Tasklist.

params.name: startablePermissionCheck
params.description:
Filter by process definitions which the user is allowed to start in Tasklist.
If the user doesn't have these permissions the result will be empty list.
The permissions are:

* `CREATE_INSTANCE` and `READ` permission on Process definition level

params.name: sortBy
params.description:

params.name: sortOrder
params.description:
Sort the results in a given order. Values may be asc for ascending order or desc for descending order.
Must be used in conjunction with the sortBy parameter.

params.description: Pagination of results. Specifies the index of the first result to return.

params.name: maxResults
params.description:

Will return less results if there are no more results left.

operations.summary: Modify the execution state of a process instance
operations.description:
Submits a list of modification instructions to change a process instance's execution state.
A modification instruction is one of the following:

* Starting execution before an activity
* Starting execution after an activity on its single outgoing sequence flow
* Starting execution on a specific sequence flow
* Canceling an activity instance, transition instance, or all instances (activity or transition) for an activity

Instructions are executed immediately and in the order they are provided in this request's body.
Variables can be provided with every starting instruction.

The exact semantics of modification can be read about in the [User guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/develop/user-guide/process-engine/process-instance-modification/).

fields.name: processDefinitionId

fields.name: processDefinitionKey

fields.name: processInstanceIds

operations.description:
A signal is an event of global scope (broadcast semantics) and is delivered to all
active handlers. Internally this maps to the engine's signal event received builder
method `RuntimeService#createSignalEvent()`. For more information about the signal
behavior, see the [Signal Events](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/bpmn20/events/signal-events/)
section of the [BPMN 2.0 Implementation Reference](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/bpmn20/).

fields.name: name
fields.description:
The name of the signal to deliver.

**Note**: This property is mandatory.

fields.name: executionId
fields.description:
Optionally specifies a single execution which is notified by the signal.

**Note**: If no execution id is defined the signal is broadcasted to all subscribed
handlers.

fields.name: tenantId
fields.description:
Specifies a tenant to deliver the signal. The signal can only be received on
executions or process definitions which belongs to the given tenant.

**Note**: Cannot be used in combination with executionId.

fields.name: withoutTenantId
fields.description:
If true the signal can only be received on executions or process definitions which
belongs to no tenant. Value may not be false as this is the default behavior.

**Note**: Cannot be used in combination with `executionId`.

operations.summary: Get the form key of a task
operations.description:
Retrieves the form key for a task. The form key corresponds to the `FormData#formKey`
property in the engine. This key can be used to do task-specific form rendering in
client applications. Additionally, the context path of the containing process
application is returned.

operations.name: get-form

operations.description:
Retrieves the form variables for a task. The form variables take form data specified
on the task into account. If form fields are defined, the variable types and default
values of the form fields are taken into account.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the task to retrieve the variables for.

params.name: variableNames
params.description:
A comma-separated list of variable names. Allows restricting the list of requested
variables to the variable names in the list. It is best practice to restrict the
list of variables to the variables actually required by the form in order to
minimize fetching of data. If the query parameter is ommitted all variables are
fetched. If the query parameter contains non-existent variable names, the variable
names are ignored.

params.name: deserializeValues
params.description:
Determines whether serializable variable values (typically variables that store
custom Java objects) should be deserialized on server side (default true).

If set to true, a serializable variable will be deserialized on server side and
transformed to JSON using [Jackson's](http://jackson.codehaus.org/) POJO/bean
property introspection feature. Note that this requires the Java classes of the
variable value to be on the REST API's classpath.

If set to false, a serializable variable will be returned in its serialized format.
For example, a variable that is serialized as XML will be returned as a JSON string
containing XML.

Note: While true is the default value for reasons of backward compatibility, we
recommend setting this parameter to false when developing web applications that are
independent of the Java process applications deployed to the engine.

responses.description: Request successful. A JSON object containing a property for each variable returned.

retrieved by using the Get Task Count method.

for custom code in the user guide for details.

params.name: followUpBeforeExpression

params.name: createdBefore

params.name: updatedAfterExpression
params.description:
Restrict to tasks that were updated after the date described by the given expression. Every action that fires
a [task update event](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/delegation-code/#task-listener-event-lifecycle) is considered as updating the task.
See the
[user guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/expression-language/#internal-context-functions)
for more information on available functions. The expression must evaluate to a
`java.util.Date` or `org.joda.time.DateTime` object.

params.name: delegationState
params.description:
Restrict to tasks that are in the given delegation state. Valid values are
`PENDING` and `RESOLVED`.

params.name: candidateGroups
params.description:
Restrict to tasks that are offered to any of the given candidate groups. Takes a
comma-separated list of group names, so for example `developers,support,sales`.

params.name: candidateGroupsExpression
params.description:
Restrict to tasks that are offered to any of the candidate groups described by the
given expression. See the
[user guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/expression-language/#internal-context-functions)
for more information on available functions. The expression must evaluate to
`java.util.List` of Strings.

params.name: withCandidateGroups
params.description:
Only include tasks which have a candidate group. Value may only be `true`,
as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: withoutCandidateGroups
params.description:
Only include tasks which have no candidate group. Value may only be `true`,
as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: withCandidateUsers
params.description:
Only include tasks which have a candidate user. Value may only be `true`,
as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: withoutCandidateUsers
params.description:
Only include tasks which have no candidate users. Value may only be `true`,
as `false` is the default behavior.

params.name: active
params.description:
Only include active tasks. Value may only be `true`, as `false`
is the default behavior.

params.name: suspended
params.description:
Only include suspended tasks. Value may only be `true`, as
`false` is the default behavior.

params.name: taskVariables
processVariables
caseInstanceVariables
variableNamesIgnoreCase
params.description:
Match all variable names in this query case-insensitively. If set
`variableName` and `variablename` are treated as equal.

params.name: variableValuesIgnoreCase
params.description:
Match all variable values in this query case-insensitively. If set
`variableValue` and `variablevalue` are treated as equal.

params.name: parentTaskId
params.description: Restrict query to all tasks that are sub tasks of the given task. Takes a task id.

params.name: withCommentAttachmentInfo
params.description:
Check if task has attachments and/or comments. Value may only be `true`, as
`false` is the default behavior.
Adding the filter will do additional attachment and comments queries to the database,
it might slow down the query in case of tables having high volume of data.
This param is not considered for count queries

params.name: withTaskVariablesInReturn
params.description:
Indicates if all the variables visible from task should be retrieved. A variable is visible from the task
if it is a local task variable or declared in a parent scope of the task. Value may only be `true`, as
`false` is the default behavior.

params.name: withTaskLocalVariablesInReturn
params.description:
Indicates if all the local variables visible from task should be retrieved. Value may only be `true`, as
`false` is the default behavior.

params.name: sortBy
params.description:
Sort the results lexicographically by a given criterion.
Must be used in conjunction with the sortOrder parameter.

params.name: sortOrder
params.description:
Sort the results in a given order. Values may be asc for ascending order or desc for descending order.
Must be used in conjunction with the sortBy parameter.

params.name: firstResult
params.description: Pagination of results. Specifies the index of the first result to return.

params.name: maxResults
params.description:
Pagination of results. Specifies the maximum number of results to return.
Will return less results if there are no more results left.

operations.name: list

operations.summary: List tasks (filters in the JSON body)
operations.description:
Queries for tasks that fulfill a given filter. This method is slightly more powerful
than the [Get Tasks](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/task/get-query/) method because it
allows filtering by multiple process or task variables of types `String`, `Number`
or `Boolean`. The size of the result set can be retrieved by using the
[Get Task Count (POST)](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/task/post-query-count/) method.

**Security Consideration**:
There are several parameters (such as `assigneeExpression`) for specifying an EL
expression. These are disabled by default to prevent remote code execution. See the
section on
[security considerations for custom code](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/securing-custom-code/)
in the user guide for details.

instance ids.

fields.name: tenantIdIn

fields.name: assignee
fields.description: Restrict to tasks that the given user is assigned to.

fields.name: assigneeExpression
fields.description:
Restrict to tasks that the user described by the given expression is assigned to. See the
[user guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/expression-language/#internal-context-functions) 
for more information on available functions.

fields.name: assigneeLike
fields.description:
Restrict to tasks that have an assignee that has the parameter 
value as a substring.

fields.name: assigneeLikeExpression
fields.description:
Restrict to tasks that have an assignee that has the parameter value described by the 
given expression as a substring. See the 
[user guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/expression-language/#internal-context-functions) 
for more information on available functions.

fields.name: assigneeIn
fields.description: Only include tasks which are assigned to one of the passed and comma-separated user ids.

fields.name: assigneeNotIn
fields.description: Only include tasks which are not assigned to one of the passed and comma-separated user ids.

fields.name: owner
fields.description: Restrict to tasks that the given user owns.

fields.name: ownerExpression
fields.description:
Restrict to tasks that the user described by the given expression owns. See the 
[user guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/expression-language/#internal-context-functions) 
for more information on available functions.

fields.name: candidateGroup
fields.description: Only include tasks that are offered to the given group.

fields.name: candidateGroupLike
fields.description: Only include tasks that are offered to groups that have the parameter value as a substring.

fields.name: candidateGroupExpression
fields.description:
Only include tasks that are offered to the group described by the given expression.

[user guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/expression-language/#internal-context-functions) 
for more information on available functions.

fields.name: candidateUser
fields.description: Only include tasks that are offered to the given user or to one of his groups.

fields.name: candidateUserExpression
fields.description:
Only include tasks that are offered to the user described by the given expression. 
See the 
[user guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/expression-language/#internal-context-functions) 
for more information on available functions.

fields.name: includeAssignedTasks
fields.description:
Also include tasks that are assigned to users in candidate queries. Default is to only 
include tasks that are not assigned to any user if you query by candidate user or
group(s).

fields.name: involvedUser
fields.description:
Only include tasks that the given user is involved in. A user is involved in a task if 
an identity link exists between task and user (e.g., the user is the assignee).

fields.name: involvedUserExpression
fields.description:
Only include tasks that the user described by the given expression is involved in.
A user is involved in a task if an identity link exists between task and user
(e.g., the user is the assignee). See the
[user guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/expression-language/#internal-context-functions)
for more information on available functions.

fields.name: assigned

fields.name: unassigned

fields.name: taskDefinitionKeyNotIn

fields.name: taskDefinitionKeyLike

fields.name: name

`java.util.Date` or `org.joda.time.DateTime` object.

fields.name: dueAfter

the format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, e.g., `2013-01-23T14:42:45.435+0200`.

fields.name: dueAfterExpression
fields.description:

[user guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/expression-language/#internal-context-functions)
for more information on available functions. The expression must evaluate to a
`java.util.Date` or `org.joda.time.DateTime` object.

fields.name: dueBefore
fields.description:
Restrict to tasks that are due before the given date. By
[default](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/overview/date-format/), the date must have
the format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, e.g., `2013-01-23T14:42:45.243+0200`.

fields.name: dueBeforeExpression

See the
[user guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/expression-language/#internal-context-functions)

`java.util.Date` or `org.joda.time.DateTime` object.

fields.name: withoutDueDate

fields.name: followUpDate

must have the format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, e.g., `2013-01-23T14:42:45.342+0200`.

fields.name: followUpDateExpression

[user guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/expression-language/#internal-context-functions)

`java.util.Date` or `org.joda.time.DateTime` object.

fields.name: followUpAfter

the format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, e.g., `2013-01-23T14:42:45.542+0200`.

fields.name: followUpAfterExpression

expression. See the
[user guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/expression-language/#internal-context-functions)
for more information on available functions. The expression must evaluate to a
`java.util.Date` or `org.joda.time.DateTime` object.

fields.name: followUpBefore

[default](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/overview/date-format/), the date must have
the format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, e.g., `2013-01-23T14:42:45.234+0200`.

fields.name: followUpBeforeExpression

expression. See the
[user guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/expression-language/#internal-context-functions)

fields.name: followUpBeforeOrNotExistentExpression

described by the given expression. See the
[user guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/expression-language/#internal-context-functions)

`java.util.Date` or `org.joda.time.DateTime` object.

fields.name: createdOn

[default](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/overview/date-format/), the date must have
the format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, e.g., `2013-01-23T14:42:45.324+0200`.

fields.name: createdOnExpression

for more information on available functions. The expression must evaluate to a
`java.util.Date` or `org.joda.time.DateTime` object.

have the format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, e.g., `2013-01-23T14:42:45.342+0200`.

fields.name: createdAfterExpression

`java.util.Date` or `org.joda.time.DateTime` object.

have the format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, e.g., `2013-01-23T14:42:45.332+0200`.

fields.name: createdBeforeExpression
fields.description:
Restrict to tasks that were created before the date described by the given expression.
See the
[user guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/expression-language/#internal-context-functions)
for more information on available functions. The expression must evaluate to a
`java.util.Date` or `org.joda.time.DateTime` object.

have the format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, e.g., `2013-01-23T14:42:45.332+0200`.

fields.name: updatedAfterExpression
fields.description:
Restrict to tasks that were updated after the date described by the given expression. Every action that fires 
a [task update event](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/delegation-code/#task-listener-event-lifecycle) is considered as updating the task.
See the
[user guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/expression-language/#internal-context-functions)
for more information on available functions. The expression must evaluate to a
`java.util.Date` or `org.joda.time.DateTime` object.

fields.name: withoutCandidateGroups

operations.name: query-count

operations.description:
Resolves a task and updates execution variables.

Resolving a task marks that the assignee is done with the task delegated to them, and
that it can be sent back to the owner. Can only be executed when the task has been
delegated. The assignee will be set to the owner, who performed the delegation.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the task to resolve.

fields.name: withVariablesInReturn
fields.description:
Indicates whether the response should contain the process variables or not. The
default is `false` with a response code of `204`. If set to `true` the response
contains the process variables and has a response code of `200`. If the task is not
associated with a process instance (e.g. if it's part of a case instance) no
variables will be returned.

**Note:** The difference with the [Claim Task](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/reference/rest/task/post-claim/)
method is that this method does not check if the task already has a user
assigned to it.

params.name: id

operations.summary: Submit the form of a task
operations.description:
Completes a task and updates process variables using a form submit. There are two
difference between this method and the `complete` method:

* If the task is in state `PENDING` - i.e., has been delegated before, it is not
completed but resolved. Otherwise it will be completed.
* If the task has Form Field Metadata defined, the process engine will perform backend
validation for any form fields which have validators defined.
See the
[Generated Task Forms](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/task-forms/_index/#generated-task-forms)
section of the [User Guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/) for more information.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the task to submit the form for.

fields.name: withVariablesInReturn
fields.description:
Indicates whether the response should contain the process variables or not. The
default is `false` with a response code of `204`. If set to `true` the response
contains the process variables and has a response code of `200`. If the task is not
associated with a process instance (e.g. if it's part of a case instance) no
variables will be returned.

responses.description: Request successful. The response contains the process variables.
Request successful. The response contains no variables.

operations.name: update

operations.description:
Adds an identity link to a task by id. Can be used to link any user or group to a task
and specify a relation.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the task to add a link to.

fields.name: userId
fields.description: The id of the user participating in this link. Either `userId` or `groupId` is set.

fields.name: groupId
fields.description: The id of the group participating in this link. Either `groupId` or `userId` is set.

fields.name: type
fields.description:
The type of the identity link. The value of the this property can be user-defined. The Process Engine
provides three pre-defined Identity Link `type`s:

* `candidate`
* `assignee` - reserved for the task assignee
* `owner` - reserved for the task owner

**Note**: When adding or removing an Identity Link, the `type` property must be defined.

params.description:
Determines whether serializable variable values (typically variables that store custom Java objects)
should be deserialized on the server side (default `true`).

If set to `true`, a serializable variable will be deserialized on server side and transformed to JSON
using [Jackson's](https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson) POJO/bean property introspection feature.
Note that this requires the Java classes of the variable value to be on the REST API's classpath.

If set to `false`, a serializable variable will be returned in its serialized format.
For example, a variable that is serialized as XML will be returned as a JSON string containing XML.

Note: While `true` is the default value for reasons of backward compatibility, we recommend setting this
parameter to `false` when developing web applications that are independent of the Java process
applications deployed to the engine.

params.name: variableValues
params.description:
Only include variable instances that have the certain values.
Value filtering expressions are comma-separated and are structured as
follows:

A valid parameter value has the form `key_operator_value`.
`key` is the variable name, `operator` is the comparison operator to be used
and `value` the variable value.

**Note:** Values are always treated as `String` objects on server side.

Valid operator values are: `eq` - equal to; `neq` - not equal to; `gt` -
greater than;
`gteq` - greater than or equal to; `lt` - lower than; `lteq` - lower than or
equal to;
`like`.
`key` and `value` may not contain underscore or comma characters.

**variableName** and **variablename** are treated as equal.

`true` **variableValue** and **variablevalue** are treated as equal.

params.name: deserializeValues
params.description:
Determines whether serializable variable values (typically variables that
store custom Java objects) should be deserialized on server side (default
`true`).

If set to `true`, a serializable variable will be deserialized on server side
and transformed to JSON using
[Jackson's](https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson) POJO/bean property
introspection feature. Note that this requires the Java classes of the
variable value to be on the REST API's classpath.

If set to `false`, a serializable variable will be returned in its serialized
format. For example, a variable that is serialized as XML will be returned as
a JSON string containing XML.

**Note:** While `true` is the default value for reasons of backward
compatibility, we recommend setting this parameter to `false` when developing
web applications that are independent of the Java process applications
deployed to the engine.

variables.description:

The array consists of objects with the three properties `name`, `operator`
and `value`.
`name (String)` is the variable name, `operator (String)` is the comparison
operator to be used and `value` the variable value.
`value` may be `String`, `Number` or `Boolean`.

Valid operator values are: `eq` - equal to; `neq` - not equal to; `gt` -
greater than;
`gteq` - greater than or equal to; `lt` - lower than; `lteq` - lower than or
equal to;
`like`.

and `value`.

operator to be used and `value` the variable value.

variables.description:
A JSON array to only include process instances that have/had variables with certain values.
The array consists of objects with the three properties `name`, `operator` and `value`. `name` (`String`) is the variable name,
`operator` (`String`) is the comparison operator to be used and `value` the variable value.

Value may be `String`, `Number` or `Boolean`.

Valid operator values are: `eq` - equal to; `neq` - not equal to; `gt` - greater than; `gteq` - greater than or equal to; `lt` - lower than; `lteq` - lower than or equal to; `like`.

variableNamesIgnoreCase.description: Match all variable names provided in variables case-insensitively. If set to `true` variableName and variablename are treated as equal.

variableValuesIgnoreCase.description: Match all variable values provided in variables case-insensitively. If set to `true` variableValue and variablevalue are treated as equal.

orQueries.description:
A JSON array of nested historic process instance queries with OR semantics.

A process instance matches a nested query if it fulfills at least one of the query's predicates.

With multiple nested queries, a process instance must fulfill at least one predicate of each query
([Conjunctive Normal Form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjunctive_normal_form)).

All process instance query properties can be used except for: `sorting`

See the [User Guide](https://docs.operaton.org/manual/1.0/user-guide/process-engine/process-engine-api/#or-queries) for more information about OR queries.

descending order. Must be used in conjunction with the sortBy parameter.
